selection.reason: Batched handoff produced a modest measured CPU saving with essentially unchanged render use. Immutable upload reduced upload operations but did not improve measured whole-player CPU or render use and had higher sampled service memory; leave it disabled.

retained_VM_runtime_audit.scope: Verified live per-boot test binary bind mount and service override, not a reboot-persistent LibreELEC release image.

limits: Exact picture and semantic Dolby payload equality is established for the three matched captured source frames per isolated option, not all media or Dolby conformance.
All eight steady observation windows had no drops, skips or stalls. One batched enabled case had a raw startup/seek skip; every immutable case had zero raw drops/skips.
All eight process exits were normal. The preexisting DV display restoration failure occurred in every case and remains separately reported; this is not claimed fixed.
Performance cases exclude capture readbacks and visible subtitles; original subtitle settings were restored.
CPU is whole Kodi normalized to one core. GPU is capacity-normalized Kodi DRM client activity. Memory is sampled whole-service usage, not process RSS; lifetime peak is not interval-only.
The FFmpeg9 VAAPI/QSV decode-only comparison is public separately. Actual Kodi QSV playback remains a separate unfinished task.
